title: Artificial Learning Dynamics Atlas
scope: Curated topic and project relationships; no universal equivalence or inferred causal direction.
layoutNote: Positions group topics by cluster for navigation. Distance is not an evidence measurement.

nodes.name: Linear & ridge regression
nodes.authors: Rasmussen · Williams (Bayesian reference)
nodes.text: A linear predictor with optional quadratic regularization. Under Gaussian noise and a Gaussian weight prior, ridge matches the posterior mean and mode.
nodes.handle: An explicit coefficient map; Gaussian likelihood and prior connect ridge to Bayesian estimation ([Rasmussen and Williams](https://gaussianprocess.org/gpml/chapters/RW2.pdf)).
nodes.boundary: Inspectable coefficients describe the fitted predictor, not necessarily causal effects; its uncertainty depends on the model assumptions ([GPML](https://gaussianprocess.org/gpml/chapters/RW2.pdf)).
nodes.test: Intervene on actual inputs, break correlations, and check whether coefficient-based predictions remain valid. Compare to unregularized and sparse linear models.

nodes.name: SVMs & kernel methods
nodes.authors: Cortes · Vapnik; Rasmussen · Williams
nodes.text: Kernel-based regularized learning. SVM margin objectives differ from regression likelihoods and do not automatically provide calibrated uncertainty.
nodes.handle: The kernel specifies similarity and the margin specifies a classification objective; this makes the hypothesis class and decision rule explicit ([Cortes and Vapnik](https://research.google/pubs/support-vector-networks/), [Rasmussen and Williams](https://gaussianprocess.org/gpml/chapters/RW6.pdf)).
nodes.boundary: A margin in feature space is not calibrated probability or a causal state variable; the kernel defines what differences count as small ([GPML](https://gaussianprocess.org/gpml/chapters/RW6.pdf)).
nodes.test: Test perturbations in physical/task coordinates, not only kernel distance; compare an explicit feature model with the nonlinear kernel.

nodes.name: Gaussian processes
nodes.authors: Rasmussen · Williams
nodes.text: A probability distribution over functions. Kernel regression and Bayesian prediction connect under Gaussian assumptions.
nodes.handle: Posterior means and covariance expose a model of uncertainty; GP-based dynamics can support conditional safe-learning certificates ([Rasmussen and Williams](https://gaussianprocess.org/gpml/chapters/RW2.pdf), [Berkenkamp, Turchetta, Schoellig, and Krause](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1705.08551)).
nodes.boundary: The safe-learning theorem needs uniform confidence coverage and regularity, not merely a plotted posterior interval; the experiment relaxes parts of the theoretical setup ([Berkenkamp et al.](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1705.08551)).
nodes.test: Test simultaneous coverage across adaptively visited states and challenge the kernel with an omitted dynamics regime.

nodes.name: k-means & quantization
nodes.authors: Lloyd · MacQueen · Hartigan · Wong
nodes.text: Minimize within-cluster squared distance. This is a clustering or quantization objective, not a transition model by itself.
nodes.handle: Centroids and assignments give an explicit partition minimizing within-cluster squared distances ([Lloyd, MacQueen, Hartigan, and Wong lineage](https://web.mit.edu/r/current/lib/R/library/stats/html/kmeans.html)).
nodes.boundary: A geometric partition has no action-conditioned transition model; distance-based clustering alone does not supply a control state ([R documentation](https://web.mit.edu/r/current/lib/R/library/stats/html/kmeans.html)).
nodes.test: Within each cluster, apply the same actions and test whether rewards, constraints, and future observations agree. Split clusters when they do not.

nodes.name: Trees & ensembles
nodes.authors: Grinsztajn · Oyallon · Varoquaux (benchmark)
nodes.text: Non-neural baselines remain important. A 45-dataset study found favorable tree performance on medium-sized tabular data, not universal dominance.
nodes.handle: A small tree exposes decision predicates; ensembles are useful predictive baselines but need not remain easy to inspect ([Hastie, Tibshirani, and Friedman](https://hastie.su.domains/ElemStatLearn/main.html)).
nodes.boundary: Good tabular prediction does not establish causal or temporal correctness; favorable tree benchmarks concern specified datasets, not universal superiority ([Grinsztajn, Oyallon, and Varoquaux](https://arxiv.org/abs/2207.08815)).
nodes.test: Compare a compact tree, boosted ensemble, and neural predictor on intervention response and shifted operating regimes, not just random-split accuracy.

nodes.name: Latent-variable models
nodes.authors: Watanabe; Särkkä · Svensson
nodes.text: Unobserved components or states create inference and identifiability questions. Mixtures and HMMs are among the singular models analyzed by SLT.
nodes.handle: Explicit emission and transition models make probabilistic assumptions inspectable; filtering computes beliefs about unobserved state ([Särkkä and Svensson](https://users.aalto.fi/~ssarkka/pub/bfs_book_2023_online.pdf)).
nodes.boundary: Latent representations can be non-identifiable; observations alone need not choose the intended semantic factors ([Locatello et al.](https://www.arxiv.org/pdf/2007.14184)).
nodes.test: Construct observationally equivalent alternatives and seek an action, sensor, or intervention that distinguishes them.

nodes.name: Convolution & digital filters
nodes.authors: Oppenheim · Schafer (teaching lineage)
nodes.text: Impulse responses, difference equations, Fourier analysis, and FIR/IIR filters describe signal transformations. Fixed linear SSMs admit convolutional evaluation.
nodes.handle: Impulse responses and frequency responses specify signal transformations; LTI state-space layers also admit convolutional evaluation ([Oppenheim and Schafer teaching lineage](https://ocw.mit.edu/courses/res-6-dtsp-discrete-time-signal-processing/pages/signal-processing-courses/), [Gu, Goel, and Ré](https://arxiv.org/html/2111.00396v3)).
nodes.boundary: Filter stability or attenuation says what happens to signals, not whether a task-relevant event was preserved ([MIT DSP](https://ocw.mit.edu/courses/res-6-dtsp-discrete-time-signal-processing/pages/signal-processing-courses/)).
nodes.test: Inject known signals and hazards across frequencies; measure attenuation, delay, and missed-event cost.

nodes.name: Fourier & spectral analysis
nodes.authors: Oppenheim · Schafer (reference)
nodes.text: Frequency-domain representations support filtering, spectral analysis, and efficient convolutions. They are mathematical tools, not a single learning architecture.
nodes.handle: Explicit spectral representations support filter and feedback-loop analysis ([Oppenheim and Schafer](https://ocw.mit.edu/courses/res-6-dtsp-discrete-time-signal-processing/pages/signal-processing-courses/), [Åström and Murray](https://people.duke.edu/~hpgavin/SystemID/References/Astrom-Feedback-2006.pdf)).
nodes.boundary: Spectral information is a mathematical description, not a semantic decomposition; feedback stability depends on the complete loop ([Åström and Murray](https://people.duke.edu/~hpgavin/SystemID/References/Astrom-Feedback-2006.pdf)).
nodes.test: Measure phase and gain under actual sample rates, delays, and actuator saturation, then compare with the predicted loop behavior.

nodes.name: Wavelets & multiresolution
nodes.authors: Stéphane Mallat
nodes.text: Orthogonal scale-dependent approximation and detail signals. Filter banks provide the computational construction.
nodes.handle: Scale-specific filtering is explicit; scattering networks add prescribed wavelet/modulus operations with nonexpansiveness and deformation bounds under stated conditions ([Mallat](https://www.di.ens.fr/~mallat/papiers/MallatTheory89.pdf), [Bruna and Mallat](https://www.di.ens.fr/~mallat/papiers/Bruna-Mallat-Pami-Scat.pdf)).
nodes.boundary: Representation stability is not classification correctness, and finite averaging deliberately discards information ([Bruna and Mallat](https://www.di.ens.fr/~mallat/papiers/Bruna-Mallat-Pami-Scat.pdf)).
nodes.test: Vary nuisance deformations and task-critical fine structure separately; test whether the chosen invariant removes information needed for control.

nodes.name: Wiener filtering
nodes.authors: Norbert Wiener
nodes.text: Filtering, extrapolation, interpolation, and smoothing of stationary time series. Kalman's work recasts the estimation problem in state-space form.
nodes.handle: A stochastic linear-estimation problem can be solved using signal and noise statistics ([Wiener](https://direct.mit.edu/books/oa-monograph/4361/chapter/187129/Introduction), [Kalman](https://www.cs.cmu.edu/~motionplanning/papers/sbp_papers/k/Kalman1960.pdf)).
nodes.boundary: Optimality is relative to the estimator class and statistical assumptions, not arbitrary nonlinear or nonstationary environments ([Kalman](https://www.cs.cmu.edu/~motionplanning/papers/sbp_papers/k/Kalman1960.pdf)).
nodes.test: Shift noise spectra and event rates; compare causal filtering, delayed smoothing, and downstream control error.

nodes.name: Kalman & Kalman–Bucy filters
nodes.authors: Rudolf Kalman · Richard Bucy
nodes.text: Recursive state and covariance estimation. Linear-Gaussian filtering is exact; nonlinear inference needs additional approximation.
nodes.handle: Explicit states, measurement maps, innovations, and covariance updates expose the estimator; linear-Gaussian filtering is exact ([Kalman](https://www.cs.cmu.edu/~motionplanning/papers/sbp_papers/k/Kalman1960.pdf), [Kalman and Bucy](https://people.duke.edu/~hpgavin/SystemID/References/KalmanBucy-ASME-JBE-1961.pdf)).
nodes.boundary: State estimation is not actuation; uncertainty and observer performance depend on observability and the dynamics/noise model ([Särkkä and Svensson](https://users.aalto.fi/~ssarkka/pub/bfs_book_2023_online.pdf)).
nodes.test: Check innovation consistency, sensor bias, unobservable modes, and actuator loss before claiming successful feedback control.

nodes.name: Nonlinear Bayesian filtering
nodes.authors: Särkkä · Svensson (reference)
nodes.text: Extended, unscented, cubature, and particle methods approximate inference beyond linear-Gaussian models. Filtering and smoothing condition on different observation intervals.
nodes.handle: Nonlinear Bayesian estimation exposes a belief rather than pretending one point state is certain; different approximations handle different posterior shapes ([Särkkä and Svensson](https://users.aalto.fi/~ssarkka/pub/bfs_book_2023_online.pdf)).
nodes.boundary: Approximation error, particle degeneracy, and model mismatch matter; smoothing uses future data unavailable to an online controller ([Särkkä and Svensson](https://users.aalto.fi/~ssarkka/pub/bfs_book_2023_online.pdf)).
nodes.test: Compare posterior coverage and failure detection with an exact small-system reference; evaluate online and hindsight estimates separately.

nodes.name: Bilateral image filtering
nodes.authors: Carlo Tomasi · Roberto Manduchi
nodes.text: Spatial closeness and pixel-value similarity determine normalized averaging weights. Content dependence resembles attention, but does not establish equivalence.
nodes.handle: Spatial and intensity similarity explicitly govern edge-preserving averaging ([Tomasi and Manduchi](https://www.cs.jhu.edu/~misha/ReadingSeminar/Papers/Tomasi98.pdf)).
nodes.boundary: Preserving image edges is not preserving objects, small hazards, or physically meaningful boundaries ([Tomasi and Manduchi](https://www.cs.jhu.edu/~misha/ReadingSeminar/Papers/Tomasi98.pdf)).
nodes.test: Change contrast, lighting, and sensor noise while holding geometry fixed; measure the effect on estimated clearance and object identity.

nodes.name: Anisotropic diffusion
nodes.authors: Pietro Perona · Jitendra Malik
nodes.text: A spatially varying diffusion coefficient encourages smoothing within regions rather than across edges. This is not generative reverse diffusion.
nodes.handle: An explicit PDE and diffusivity function regulate spatial smoothing ([Perona and Malik](https://openreview.net/forum?id=R2gc38YmhX)).
nodes.boundary: Image-evolution time is not physical time; edge-sensitive smoothing does not establish a correct scene model ([Perona and Malik](https://openreview.net/forum?id=R2gc38YmhX)).
nodes.test: Audit the numerical discretization and test whether small task-critical boundaries survive the full perception-to-action pipeline.

nodes.name: Convolutional networks
nodes.authors: LeCun · Bottou · Bengio · Haffner
nodes.text: Learned filters composed with nonlinear processing. A convolutional layer and an entire CNN should not be treated as the same linear operator.
nodes.handle: Local weight sharing gives a designed spatial structure; fixed scattering provides a related construction with stronger specified signal guarantees ([LeCun, Bottou, Bengio, and Haffner](https://leon.bottou.org/papers/lecun-98h), [Bruna and Mallat](https://www.di.ens.fr/~mallat/papiers/Bruna-Mallat-Pami-Scat.pdf)).
nodes.boundary: A learned filter stack does not inherit every scattering guarantee; structural locality is not object-level meaning ([Bruna and Mallat](https://www.di.ens.fr/~mallat/papiers/Bruna-Mallat-Pami-Scat.pdf)).
nodes.test: Train matched CNN, scattering-plus-readout, and equivariant models; separate geometric robustness from concept and intervention accuracy.

nodes.name: Recurrent neural networks
nodes.authors: Jeffrey Elman (simple-RNN anchor)
nodes.text: A recurrent hidden state carries previous activity into the next input step. A predictive memory need not be a physically identified state.
nodes.handle: The recurrence is a learned dynamical system; contraction constraints bound sensitivity and imply fading dependence on initial state ([Elman](https://pages.ucsd.edu/~rbelew/courses/readings/elman90-fsit.pdf), [Miller and Hardt](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1805.10369)).
nodes.boundary: A stable recurrence can forget information that the task needs; hidden state is not automatically an identified world state ([Miller and Hardt](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1805.10369)).
nodes.test: Combine long-delay memory tasks with perturbation recovery, and measure whether a correction survives without erasing unrelated knowledge.

nodes.name: LSTM & GRU
nodes.authors: Hochreiter · Schmidhuber; Cho et al.
nodes.text: Gated recurrent memory. LSTM was designed to preserve useful error flow across long intervals; gates are not automatically Bayesian uncertainty weights.
nodes.handle: Gates create adjustable memory paths; sufficient contraction conditions have been studied for LSTMs ([Hochreiter and Schmidhuber](https://mlanthology.org/neco/1997/hochreiter1997neco-long/), [Cho et al.](https://www.arxiv.org/abs/1406.1078), [Miller and Hardt](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1805.10369)).
nodes.boundary: The cited LSTM conditions are restrictive and do not constitute a universal theorem for all LSTMs or GRUs; gates are not inherently interpretable Bayesian gains ([Miller and Hardt](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1805.10369)).
nodes.test: Test gate-constrained and unconstrained versions on retained instructions, noise rejection, and contradictory late evidence at matched compute.

nodes.name: Transformers & attention
nodes.authors: Vaswani · Shazeer · Parmar · Uszkoreit · Jones · Gomez · Kaiser · Polosukhin
nodes.text: Attention-based sequence transduction. Standard softmax attention is not universally an exact fixed-size recurrent state-space computation.
nodes.handle: Attention, context construction, objectives, and interfaces can be designed explicitly; behavior can be shaped through instruction training ([Vaswani et al.](https://arxiv.org/abs/1706.03762v5), [Ouyang et al.](https://arxiv.org/abs/2203.02155)).
nodes.boundary: Architecture specification does not identify semantic variables; instruction-following improvements are empirical, not all-input compliance guarantees ([Ouyang et al.](https://arxiv.org/abs/2203.02155)).
nodes.test: Train on counterfactual instruction conflicts and held-out compositions; assess capability and correction retention without inspecting circuits.

nodes.name: Linear attention
nodes.authors: Katharopoulos · Vyas · Pappas · Fleuret
nodes.text: Kernel-feature attention permits recurrent evaluation using associative accumulation. This changes or approximates the standard attention construction.
nodes.handle: Feature-map attention permits recurrent sufficient accumulations for the chosen attention formula ([Katharopoulos, Vyas, Pappas, and Fleuret](https://proceedings.mlr.press/v119/katharopoulos20a.html)).
nodes.boundary: An efficient recurrence is not proof that its compressed state preserves every future task-relevant distinction ([Katharopoulos et al.](https://proceedings.mlr.press/v119/katharopoulos20a.html)).
nodes.test: Increase distractors and delayed queries while requiring exact state tracking; compare memory errors and recovery after explicit correction.

nodes.name: Structured SSMs / S4
nodes.authors: Albert Gu · Karan Goel · Christopher Ré
nodes.text: Structured linear state-space layers have continuous, recurrent, and convolutional representations. Nonlinear composition makes the full network nonlinear.
nodes.handle: State-transition structure and discretization provide deliberate memory timescales and equivalent recurrence/convolution views ([Gu, Goel, and Ré](https://arxiv.org/html/2111.00396v3)).
nodes.boundary: A structured linear layer is not a physically identified latent model, and a nonlinear stack needs its own analysis ([Gu et al.](https://arxiv.org/html/2111.00396v3)).
nodes.test: Vary sampling intervals and task timescales; test both memory retention and identified input-output response of the whole model.

nodes.name: Selective SSMs / Mamba
nodes.authors: Albert Gu · Tri Dao
nodes.text: Input-dependent state-update parameters select what to retain. Time variation prevents a single fixed convolution kernel, and enables gated-recurrence connections.
nodes.handle: Input-dependent updates give learned retention and selection rather than one fixed filter ([Gu and Dao](https://arxiv.org/html/2312.00752v2)).
nodes.boundary: Input-dependent gating does not establish semantic editability; expressivity and trainability of state tracking need separate evidence ([Terzić et al.](https://proceedings.neurips.cc/paper_files/paper/2025/file/77b830c18836a9b2e1395a4936dd687a-Paper-Conference.pdf)).
nodes.test: Test held-out action sequences, length extrapolation, and persistent rule changes against transformer, LSTM, and symbolic-state baselines.

nodes.name: Mamba-2 & state-space duality
nodes.authors: Tri Dao · Albert Gu
nodes.text: Semiseparable matrix structure connects SSMs with attention variants. The relationship is conditional, not a universal identity of all models.
nodes.handle: Semiseparable structure gives a precise connection between SSM and attention variants ([Dao and Gu](https://arxiv.org/abs/2405.21060)).
nodes.boundary: An algebraic duality is not an alignment theorem or a statement that all attention architectures have identical behavior ([Dao and Gu](https://arxiv.org/abs/2405.21060)).
nodes.test: Hold the mathematical operator fixed across implementations, then separate numerical differences from learned behavioral differences.

nodes.name: Hyena / gated convolution
nodes.authors: Poli · Massaroli · Nguyen · Fu · Dao · Baccus · Bengio · Ermon · Ré
nodes.text: Long implicit convolutions interleave with input-dependent gates. Runtime advantages depend on length, implementation, and accelerator utilization.
nodes.handle: Long convolutions and gates provide an explicit sequence-operator design ([Poli et al.](https://proceedings.mlr.press/v202/poli23a/poli23a.pdf)).
nodes.boundary: Faster sequence processing or competitive loss does not show semantic controllability or accurate state transitions ([Poli et al.](https://proceedings.mlr.press/v202/poli23a/poli23a.pdf)).
nodes.test: Compare at matched training and inference budgets on compositional state tracking, exact retrieval, and correction persistence.

nodes.name: SSM–attention hybrids
nodes.authors: De · Smith et al. (Griffin); Lieber et al. (Jamba)
nodes.text: Combine compressed recurrent memory with explicit attention. Griffin uses gated recurrence and local attention, with documented retrieval limitations.
nodes.handle: Recurrence and explicit attention provide different memory mechanisms that can be combined ([De, Smith, and collaborators, Griffin](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2402.19427)).
nodes.boundary: A hybrid inherits neither perfect recall nor a general control guarantee; Griffin documents retrieval-related limitations ([Griffin](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2402.19427)).
nodes.test: Ablate recurrence, attention, and explicit memory while keeping data and evaluation fixed; look for complementary gains rather than added parameters alone.

nodes.name: Neural ODEs
nodes.authors: Chen · Rubanova · Bettencourt · Duvenaud
nodes.text: Learn a vector field and use an ODE solver for evolution. Physical time, network depth, and numerical discretization must remain distinct.
nodes.handle: An explicit learned vector field supports continuous-time modeling; the solver is part of the computation ([Chen, Rubanova, Bettencourt, and Duvenaud](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1806.07366)).
nodes.boundary: A vector field is not automatically stable, identifiable, or physically meaningful; numerical integration adds a separate error source ([Chen et al.](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1806.07366)).
nodes.test: Compare unconstrained, contracting, and physics-structured fields under changed step size and unseen controls; measure real rollout error.

nodes.name: Generative diffusion
nodes.authors: Sohl-Dickstein et al.; Ho · Jain · Abbeel
nodes.text: Destroy structure with a forward process and learn a reverse generative process. The noise schedule is not automatically a physical process.
nodes.handle: A known corruption process and learned denoiser define generation; classifier-free guidance creates an explicit conditioning strength ([Ho, Jain, and Abbeel](https://arxiv.org/abs/2006.11239), [Ho and Salimans](https://arxiv.org/abs/2207.12598)).
nodes.boundary: Guidance trades fidelity and diversity; it is not a guarantee that every requested property holds ([Ho and Salimans](https://arxiv.org/abs/2207.12598)).
nodes.test: Measure reachable combinations of attributes, per-attribute calibration, and diversity loss as conditioning strength changes.

nodes.name: Score SDE / probability-flow ODE
nodes.authors: Song · Sohl-Dickstein · Kingma · Kumar · Ermon · Poole
nodes.text: A reverse SDE and probability-flow ODE share time-marginal densities under exact scores and assumptions. Their path distributions differ.
nodes.handle: Scores define stochastic or deterministic distribution transport; exact-score constructions can share time marginals ([Song et al.](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2011.13456)).
nodes.boundary: Equal marginals are not equal paths; approximate inverse-problem sampling is not exact posterior or strict measurement consistency ([Song et al.](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2011.13456), [Chung et al.](https://arxiv.org/abs/2209.14687)).
nodes.test: On a tractable inverse problem, compare posterior coverage, measurement residual, and path constraints against an exact reference.

nodes.name: Flow matching
nodes.authors: Lipman · Chen · Ben-Hamu · Nickel · Le
nodes.text: Train vector fields by regression on probability paths. Simulation-free training does not mean solver-free sample generation.
nodes.handle: Train a vector field on specified probability paths; the same objective can generate action chunks ([Lipman et al.](https://arxiv.org/abs/2210.02747), [Black et al.](https://arxiv.org/html/2410.24164)).
nodes.boundary: Matching an action distribution does not certify the safety of the executed trajectory; generation time and environment time differ ([Black et al.](https://arxiv.org/html/2410.24164)).
nodes.test: Change integrator steps and execution chunk length separately; test both deadline misses and environment-state violations.

nodes.name: Schrödinger bridges
nodes.authors: De Bortoli · Thornton · Heng · Doucet
nodes.text: Entropy-regularized transport on path space links distribution steering to generative modeling. A path-space objective is not physical control certification.
nodes.handle: Path-space transport makes a distribution-steering objective explicit ([De Bortoli, Thornton, Heng, and Doucet](https://arxiv.org/abs/2106.01357)).
nodes.boundary: Reaching endpoint distributions is different from remaining in a safe set at every physical instant ([De Bortoli et al.](https://arxiv.org/abs/2106.01357), [Ames et al.](http://ames.caltech.edu/ames2019control.pdf)).
nodes.test: Add path constraints, then test whether endpoint success hides intermediate violations and how approximated dynamics change the result.

nodes.name: Diffusion transformers
nodes.authors: William Peebles · Saining Xie
nodes.text: A transformer replaces the common convolutional U-Net backbone in latent image diffusion. Backbone and generative objective are different axes.
nodes.handle: Separate the transformer backbone from the denoising objective and sampling procedure ([Peebles and Xie](https://www.wpeebles.com/DiT.html)).
nodes.boundary: Backbone scaling and generation quality do not imply stronger conditional compliance or intelligible semantic controls ([Peebles and Xie](https://www.wpeebles.com/DiT.html)).
nodes.test: Match data, compute, conditioning interface, and sampler across DiT and U-Net; evaluate joint constraint adherence, not only FID.

nodes.name: SINDy / SINDYc
nodes.authors: Steven Brunton · Joshua Proctor · J. Nathan Kutz
nodes.text: Sparse regression discovers candidate governing equations. Controlled identification includes external inputs; sparsity depends on coordinates and the library.
nodes.handle: Sparse equations expose candidate mechanisms, including control inputs; ensembles estimate selection variability ([Brunton, Proctor, and Kutz](https://arxiv.org/abs/1605.06682), [Fasel et al.](https://arxiv.org/abs/2111.10992)).
nodes.boundary: Recovery depends on the library, coordinates, excitation, and noise; sparse readable equations can still be the wrong mechanism ([Brunton et al.](https://arxiv.org/abs/1605.06682), [Fasel et al.](https://arxiv.org/abs/2111.10992)).
nodes.test: Discover dynamics on unseen systems, intervene beyond passive trajectories, and compare control utility with ridge, GP, and neural residual models.

nodes.name: Koopman embeddings
nodes.authors: Bethany Lusch · J. Nathan Kutz · Steven Brunton
nodes.text: Learn observables that evolve approximately linearly. Infinite-dimensional operator linearity does not guarantee globally exact finite-dimensional closure.
nodes.handle: Learn coordinates with approximately linear evolution; stable matrix parameterizations and conditional contraction links are available ([Lusch, Kutz, and Brunton](https://www.lri.fr/~gcharpia/deeppractice/2022/chap_5_biblio/Koopman/KoopmanAE.pdf), [Fan et al.](https://arxiv.org/html/2401.08153v2)).
nodes.boundary: Stable latent evolution transfers to the physical system only with the required embedding relation and regularity; finite-data fitting leaves invariance error ([Fan et al.](https://arxiv.org/html/2401.08153v2)).
nodes.test: Audit encoder rank, reconstruction, controlled invariance residuals, and decoded closed-loop behavior on held-out regions.

nodes.name: Hamiltonian / Lagrangian networks
nodes.authors: Greydanus · Dzamba · Yosinski; Cranmer et al.
nodes.text: Learn mechanically structured dynamics. Conservation in a vector field is conditional and does not eliminate finite-step numerical drift.
nodes.handle: Learn energy or a Lagrangian and derive dynamics from the chosen mechanical structure ([Greydanus, Dzamba, and Yosinski](https://arxiv.org/abs/1906.01563), [Cranmer et al.](https://arxiv.org/abs/2003.04630)).
nodes.boundary: Conservative structure can be an incorrect assumption for driven or dissipative systems; a continuous-time identity is not a numerical rollout guarantee ([HNN](https://arxiv.org/abs/1906.01563), [LNN](https://arxiv.org/abs/2003.04630)).
nodes.test: Introduce friction, contact, and actuation; compare conservative, dissipative, and unconstrained models using both energy balance and task success.

nodes.name: Physics-informed networks
nodes.authors: Raissi · Perdikaris · Karniadakis; Krishnapriyan et al.
nodes.text: Use physical residuals as training constraints. Published failure modes show that soft constraints can create difficult optimization.
nodes.handle: PDE residuals supply a scientific learning constraint; solution-error bounds require PDE stability/coercivity and sampling control ([Raissi, Perdikaris, and Karniadakis](https://neuralfields.cs.brown.edu/paper_4.html), [Mishra](https://ethz.ch/content/dam/ethz/special-interest/math/applied-mathematics/camlab-dam/documents/AISE2024/AISE24%2008%2009%20Physics-Informed%20Neural%20Networks%20%E2%80%93%20Theory%20Part%201%20and%202.pdf)).
nodes.boundary: Small sampled residual is not automatically small solution error; difficult optimization and failure regimes are documented ([Krishnapriyan et al.](https://arxiv.org/abs/2109.01050)).
nodes.test: Compare with a converged numerical solver; check boundary conditions, unsampled residuals, conditioning, and downstream control sensitivity.

nodes.name: FNO & DeepONet
nodes.authors: Li · Kovachki · Stuart · Anandkumar et al.; Lu · Jin · Karniadakis
nodes.text: Learn maps between input and output functions, often across PDE families. Online speed must be compared after accounting for offline training.
nodes.handle: Learn a function-to-function map across a problem family; DeepONet theory separates encoding, approximation, and reconstruction error ([Li et al.](https://arxiv.org/abs/2010.08895), [Lanthaler, Mishra, and Karniadakis](https://academic.oup.com/imatrm/article/6/1/tnac001/6542709?searchresult=1)).
nodes.boundary: Average operator approximation bounds are not pointwise closed-loop guarantees; optimization, shift, and uncertain data are not all covered by the cited analysis ([Lanthaler et al.](https://academic.oup.com/imatrm/article/6/1/tnac001/6542709?searchresult=1)).
nodes.test: Hold out boundary conditions and geometries; convert validated approximation error into the actual controller’s robustness margin.

nodes.name: Feedback & optimal control
nodes.authors: Karl Johan Åström · Richard Murray (reference)
nodes.text: Model, estimate, and steer systems with feedback. Stability, robustness, observability, and reachability are separate properties.
nodes.handle: Explicit states, observations, actuators, costs, and disturbance models support observability, reachability, stability, and robustness analysis ([Åström and Murray](https://people.duke.edu/~hpgavin/SystemID/References/Astrom-Feedback-2006.pdf)).
nodes.boundary: PID/LQR/robust or adaptive designs are conditional on the plant and operating assumptions; feedback cannot repair an undefined objective or nonexistent actuator ([Åström and Murray](https://people.duke.edu/~hpgavin/SystemID/References/Astrom-Feedback-2006.pdf)).
nodes.test: Specify the full loop, then challenge model error, delays, saturation, and sensor loss. Compare learned control against a tuned classical controller.

nodes.name: Reinforcement learning
nodes.authors: Sergey Levine (control-as-inference reference)
nodes.text: Learn decision-making from rewards and transitions. Model learning, exploration, policy optimization, and actual control outcomes require separate evaluation.
nodes.handle: Rewards and transitions define the decision problem; control-as-inference exposes connections to probabilistic learning ([Sutton and Barto](https://web.stanford.edu/class/psych209/Readings/SuttonBartoIPRLBook2ndEd.pdf), [Levine](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1805.00909v3)).
nodes.boundary: Optimizing the specified reward does not identify the intended objective; different inference formulations can even distort disturbance treatment ([Levine](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1805.00909v3)).
nodes.test: Separate reward, task outcome, and constraint measures; test a policy on adversarially selected opportunities to exploit its proxy.

nodes.name: World models / model-based RL
nodes.authors: Hafner · Pasukonis · Ba · Lillicrap
nodes.text: DreamerV3 learns a world model and trains actor-critic behavior on imagined trajectories. Evaluate learned predictions and actual environment return separately.
nodes.handle: Action-conditioned latent dynamics can support imagined policy learning; Dreamer separates world model, actor, and critic ([Hafner et al.](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41586-025-08744-2)).
nodes.boundary: Good imagined return does not prove accurate counterfactual dynamics or grounded latent semantics; the cited results are empirical ([Hafner et al.](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41586-025-08744-2)).
nodes.test: Evaluate action-conditioned calibration, long-horizon state persistence, planner exploitation of model errors, and actual environment return separately.

nodes.name: Diffusion policy
nodes.authors: Chi · Xu · Feng · Cousineau · Du · Burchfiel · Tedrake · Song
nodes.text: Generate observation-conditioned action sequences and execute them receding-horizon. Multimodal action generation has a latency cost.
nodes.handle: Observation-conditioned action sequences support multimodal imitation and receding-horizon execution ([Chi et al.](https://ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org/html/2303.04137)).
nodes.boundary: Demonstration matching and receding-horizon execution do not certify collision avoidance or correction responsiveness ([Chi et al.](https://ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org/html/2303.04137)).
nodes.test: Insert a stop instruction or new obstacle mid-chunk; measure response latency, residual motion, and safe task completion.

nodes.name: Neural filtering / KalmanNet
nodes.authors: Revach · Shlezinger · Ni · Escoriza · van Sloun · Eldar
nodes.text: A recurrent neural module augments structural state-space filtering. Learning part of an estimator does not automatically retain classical optimality.
nodes.handle: Retain a state-space estimator structure while learning part of its update, rather than replacing all estimation structure ([Revach et al.](https://arxiv.org/abs/2107.10043)).
nodes.boundary: Learned gains do not automatically inherit classical Kalman optimality or calibrated uncertainty ([Revach et al.](https://arxiv.org/abs/2107.10043)).
nodes.test: Compare analytic, learned-gain, and residual estimators under held-out noise and dynamics changes using coverage and closed-loop outcomes.

nodes.name: Dynamical systems & chaos
nodes.authors: Lorenz; Sompolinsky · Crisanti · Sommers
nodes.text: Physical chaos, random-network chaos, and optimizer dynamics are different objects. Trajectory sensitivity does not itself establish usefulness.
nodes.handle: Attractors, local sensitivity, and stability analyze evolving systems; random recurrent-network dynamics is a distinct setting ([Åström and Murray](https://people.duke.edu/~hpgavin/SystemID/References/Astrom-Feedback-2006.pdf), [Sompolinsky, Crisanti, and Sommers](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/10039285/)).
nodes.boundary: Instability of open-loop prediction does not by itself settle feedback controllability, and random-network ensemble results do not certify trained finite models ([Åström and Murray](https://people.duke.edu/~hpgavin/SystemID/References/Astrom-Feedback-2006.pdf)).
nodes.test: Compare forecast horizon, invariant statistics, and closed-loop regulation separately under measured disturbances.

nodes.name: Reservoir computing
nodes.authors: Jaeger · Haas; Pathak · Hunt · Girvan · Lu · Ott
nodes.text: Recurrent nonlinear activity with a learned readout supplies a practical baseline for forecasting chaotic systems.
nodes.handle: Fixed recurrent dynamics plus a learned readout provide a simple recurrent baseline and demonstrated chaotic forecasting ([Jaeger and Haas](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/15064413/), [Pathak et al.](https://link.aps.org/doi/10.1103/PhysRevLett.120.024102)).
nodes.boundary: A reservoir good at prediction need not expose semantic state or remain useful under intervention ([Pathak et al.](https://link.aps.org/doi/10.1103/PhysRevLett.120.024102)).
nodes.test: Train only the readout, then compare with fully trained recurrence on unseen control inputs and correction cost.

nodes.name: Low-rank RNN dynamics
nodes.authors: Francesca Mastrogiuseppe · Srdjan Ostojic
nodes.text: Random connectivity plus low-rank structure supports analytical study of low-dimensional task-relevant dynamics under ensemble assumptions.
nodes.handle: Designed low-rank connectivity supports reduced dynamical descriptions linking connectivity and computation ([Mastrogiuseppe and Ostojic](https://arxiv.org/html/1711.09672v2)).
nodes.boundary: The reduction depends on structure and ensemble assumptions; a low-dimensional coordinate is not automatically a named semantic variable ([Mastrogiuseppe and Ostojic](https://arxiv.org/html/1711.09672v2)).
nodes.test: Construct task-bearing low-rank models and test whether the reduced dynamics predicts held-out intervention responses, not just ordinary trajectories.

nodes.name: Task-trained recurrent DMFT
nodes.authors: Clark · Bordelon · Zavatone-Veth · Pehlevan
nodes.text: Large-network mean-field analysis connects task-aligned restructuring with temporal correlations. This is not a universal finite-system formula.
nodes.handle: Dynamical mean-field theory studies aggregate correlations and dynamics of large trained recurrent systems ([Clark, Bordelon, Zavatone-Veth, and Pehlevan](https://kempnerinstitute.harvard.edu/research/deeper-learning/structure-disorder-and-dynamics-in-task-trained-recurrent-neural-circuits/)).
nodes.boundary: Ensemble or large-width behavior is not a certificate for one finite model or a semantic control law ([Kempner research account](https://kempnerinstitute.harvard.edu/research/deeper-learning/structure-disorder-and-dynamics-in-task-trained-recurrent-neural-circuits/)).
nodes.test: Pre-register finite-width corrections and compare predicted response distributions with trained networks across seeds and task changes.

nodes.name: Criticality & propagation
nodes.authors: Schoenholz · Gilmer · Ganguli · Sohl-Dickstein
nodes.text: Mean-field theory relates initialization, correlations, and gradient propagation in wide feed-forward networks. Criticality is not a universal optimum.
nodes.handle: Initialization theory links propagation depth to correlations and gradients in specified wide-network regimes ([Schoenholz, Gilmer, Ganguli, and Sohl-Dickstein](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1611.01232v2)).
nodes.boundary: The analyzed critical regime is not a universal optimum for intelligence, safety, or correction reliability ([Schoenholz et al.](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1611.01232v2)).
nodes.test: Match training compute across subcritical, near-critical, and supercritical initializations; compare learned utility and intervention robustness.

nodes.name: Deep linear learning dynamics
nodes.authors: Saxe · McClelland · Ganguli
nodes.text: Factorized linear networks have nonlinear training dynamics and stage-like transitions. Nonlinear learning dynamics need not imply nonlinear forward maps.
nodes.handle: Exact reduced analyses show nonlinear, stagewise parameter learning even with a linear end-to-end map ([Saxe, McClelland, and Ganguli](https://www.saxelab.org/assets/papers/Saxe2013a.pdf)).
nodes.boundary: Solvable deep-linear dynamics do not establish analogous global laws for arbitrary nonlinear training ([Saxe et al.](https://www.saxelab.org/assets/papers/Saxe2013a.pdf)).
nodes.test: Test curriculum and data reweighting predictions first where the equations are exact, then quantify failures in nonlinear extensions.

nodes.name: Neural tangent kernel
nodes.authors: Jacot · Gabriel · Hongler
nodes.text: In an appropriate infinite-width limit, a fixed kernel describes training-time function evolution. Finite feature-learning regimes require other descriptions.
nodes.handle: In a specified infinite-width training regime, function evolution is described by a limiting kernel ([Jacot, Gabriel, and Hongler](https://arxiv.org/abs/1806.07572)).
nodes.boundary: Fixed-kernel predictions need not capture substantial feature learning; the regime must be checked, not presumed ([Jacot et al.](https://arxiv.org/abs/1806.07572)).
nodes.test: Predict a small training intervention with a kernel model and compare with actual retraining across width and training duration.

nodes.name: Information theory
nodes.authors: Claude Shannon
nodes.text: Entropy, coding, capacity, and distortion quantify statistical information under specified models. They do not directly measure semantic usefulness.
nodes.handle: Entropy, mutual information, coding, and capacity quantify specified random variables and communication channels ([Shannon](https://people.math.harvard.edu/~ctm/home/text/others/shannon/entropy/entropy.pdf)).
nodes.boundary: Information quantity alone does not define which facts or goals matter; the variables and task determine its relevance ([Shannon](https://people.math.harvard.edu/~ctm/home/text/others/shannon/entropy/entropy.pdf), [Tishby, Pereira, and Bialek](https://www.princeton.edu/~wbialek/our_papers/tishby+al_99.pdf)).
nodes.test: Specify the target before measuring information; test whether retained bits predict action consequences and necessary safety distinctions.

nodes.name: Information bottleneck
nodes.authors: Tishby · Pereira · Bialek
nodes.text: Compress input information while retaining information about a specified relevance variable. Task relevance must be defined, not assumed.
nodes.handle: Optimize compression relative to a designated relevant variable ([Tishby, Pereira, and Bialek](https://www.princeton.edu/~wbialek/our_papers/tishby+al_99.pdf)).
nodes.boundary: A general compression-causes-generalization account is not supported across all networks; estimator and nonlinearity choices matter ([Saxe, Bansal, and collaborators](https://research.ibm.com/publications/on-the-information-bottleneck-theory-of-deep-learning)).
nodes.test: Change the task and constraint targets while holding compression level fixed; test which consequential distinctions disappear.

nodes.name: Information-limited feedback
nodes.authors: Girish Nair · Robin Evans
nodes.text: A finite-rate control theorem links unstable linear modes to necessary communication rate under explicit assumptions. It is not a neural-state-size theorem.
nodes.handle: Unstable plant modes imply communication requirements for stabilization in a specified stochastic-control setting ([Nair and Evans](https://people.eng.unimelb.edu.au/gnair/NairSICON04.pdf)).
nodes.boundary: A data-rate theorem is not a universal hidden-state-size bound or an explanation of language intelligence ([Nair and Evans](https://people.eng.unimelb.edu.au/gnair/NairSICON04.pdf)).
nodes.test: Impose channel rate, latency, and packet-loss constraints on an actual loop and test the theorem’s assumptions explicitly.

nodes.name: Singular learning theory
nodes.authors: Sumio Watanabe
nodes.text: Singular geometry changes Bayesian evidence asymptotics. The real log canonical threshold is not a Lyapunov exponent or an observability rank.
nodes.handle: Bayesian evidence and generalization geometry can differ from regular parameter-count approximations ([Watanabe](https://www.jmlr.org/papers/volume14/watanabe13a/watanabe13a.pdf)).
nodes.boundary: Bayesian asymptotics under analytic/statistical conditions do not directly specify SGD trajectories, semantic objectives, or a controller ([Watanabe](https://www.jmlr.org/papers/volume14/watanabe13a/watanabe13a.pdf)).
nodes.test: Ask for one quantitative training-response prediction that beats a simpler baseline; do not treat the learning coefficient itself as safety.

nodes.name: Local learning coefficient
nodes.authors: Lau · Furman · Wang · Murfet · Wei
nodes.text: A local singularity-aware complexity measure with a sampling-based estimator. Temperature, localization, and sampling influence estimates.
nodes.handle: A localized complexity estimator connects sampled loss geometry to a local learning coefficient ([Lau, Furman, Wang, Murfet, and Wei](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2308.12108)).
nodes.boundary: Localization, temperature, sampling, and local-minimum assumptions affect interpretation; estimates are not direct semantic labels ([Lau et al.](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2308.12108)).
nodes.test: Establish estimator repeatability first, then test incremental predictive value for intervention outcomes beyond loss, gradients, and behavior.

nodes.name: Developmental learning theory
nodes.authors: Hoogland · Wang · Farrugia-Roberts · Carroll · Wei · Murfet
nodes.text: Requested developmental lineage, restricted here to statistical geometry and learning stages. No circuit or attention-head analysis is included.
nodes.handle: Training stages have been studied through loss geometry and behavioral changes; stagewise attribution analyzes changing training-data influence ([Hoogland and collaborators](https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.02364), [Lee, Smith, Adam, and Hoogland](https://arxiv.org/html/2510.12071v1)).
nodes.boundary: Detecting a stage is not controlling it; the link from Bayesian analysis to non-equilibrium SGD remains a stated limitation ([Lee et al.](https://arxiv.org/html/2510.12071v1)).
nodes.test: Select interventions using early checkpoints only; predict correction efficacy at later checkpoints and compare with ordinary validation-based selection.

nodes.name: MDL & singular compression
nodes.authors: Urdshals · Lau · Hoogland · van Wingerden · Murfet
nodes.text: Singular learning theory connects to description length; experiments relate estimated LLC to compressibility. Correlation does not establish a universal bound.
nodes.handle: Description length and singular statistical complexity have a mathematical connection under specified assumptions, with reported compression correlations ([Urdshals, Lau, Hoogland, van Wingerden, and Murfet](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2510.12077)).
nodes.boundary: Compression is not semantic preservation, and correlation with compressibility does not establish a safe-control metric ([Urdshals et al.](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2510.12077)).
nodes.test: Measure loss, capability, rare-constraint behavior, and correction retention before and after compression at matched deployment cost.

nodes.name: Hoogland’s master’s thesis
nodes.authors: Jesse Hoogland · supervisor Greg Stephens
nodes.text: The Ergodic Theory of Random Neural Networks, University of Amsterdam. Metadata verified from the author; full text not located, so no thesis-specific results are asserted.
nodes.handle: The verified title is The Ergodic Theory of Random Neural Networks; his biography lists a University of Amsterdam physics master’s in 2019–2021 and supervisor Greg Stephens ([Hoogland](https://www.jessehoogland.com/about)).
nodes.boundary: Full text was not located in the preceding investigation; no thesis-specific equations, guarantees, or findings are asserted. Ergodicity and controllability are not interchangeable definitions.
nodes.test: Obtain the thesis before tracing its actual results into training or control hypotheses. Use the independently sourced RNN and learning-theory literature meanwhile.

nodes.name: TD learning & Q-learning
nodes.authors: Sutton · Barto; Watkins · Dayan
nodes.text: Value learning from sampled rewards and transitions. Tabular convergence depends on repeated exploration, representation, and step-size assumptions.
nodes.handle: Explicit Bellman targets and tabular convergence results clarify what is being learned ([Sutton and Barto](https://web.stanford.edu/class/psych209/Readings/SuttonBartoIPRLBook2ndEd.pdf), [Watkins and Dayan](http://www.gatsby.ucl.ac.uk/~dayan/papers/wd92.html)).
nodes.boundary: Repeated sampling and step-size conditions matter; tabular convergence does not extend automatically to arbitrary nonlinear off-policy learning ([Sutton and Barto](https://web.stanford.edu/class/psych209/Readings/SuttonBartoIPRLBook2ndEd.pdf)).
nodes.test: Start with an exact solvable reference, then add approximation and off-policy shift one at a time; diagnose value error versus decision error.

nodes.name: Policy gradients / PPO / SAC
nodes.authors: Schulman et al.; Haarnoja · Zhou · Abbeel · Levine
nodes.text: Policy optimization and actor-critic methods learn action choices. Empirical optimization success does not imply physical stability or safety guarantees.
nodes.handle: Differentiable policy objectives, surrogates, and entropy regularization supply concrete learning levers ([Schulman et al.](https://www.arxiv.org/abs/1707.06347), [Haarnoja et al.](https://github.com/haarnoja/sac)).
nodes.boundary: Clipping, KL penalties, and policy entropy are not physical safety constraints or proofs of intended behavior ([PPO](https://www.arxiv.org/abs/1707.06347), [Achiam et al.](https://proceedings.mlr.press/v70/achiam17a/achiam17a.pdf)).
nodes.test: Compare policy updates using actual constraint trajectories and rare failures, not surrogate objective improvement alone.

nodes.name: Neural CDEs
nodes.authors: Kidger · Morrill · Foster · Lyons
nodes.text: Continuous-time models for partially observed, irregularly sampled multivariate time series. The name does not certify closed-loop stability.
nodes.handle: A continuous path drives hidden-state evolution, suitable for irregular time-series modeling ([Kidger, Morrill, Foster, and Lyons](https://www.maths.ox.ac.uk/node/36672)).
nodes.boundary: “Controlled” means driven by a path in this mathematical construction; it does not itself guarantee an engineer can steer outcomes ([Kidger et al.](https://www.maths.ox.ac.uk/node/36672)).
nodes.test: Change interpolation, sample timing, and missingness independently of the physical process; require stable decision quality and justified uncertainty.

nodes.name: Graph networks
nodes.authors: Battaglia · Hamrick · Bapst · Sanchez-Gonzalez et al.
nodes.text: Relational inductive biases represent entities and their interactions. Graph structure alone does not identify a physical law.
nodes.handle: Entities and relations are explicit architectural choices, enabling relational inductive biases ([Battaglia et al.](https://arxiv.org/abs/1806.01261)).
nodes.boundary: A graph can encode the wrong entities or interactions; relational structure alone does not establish causal or physical truth ([Battaglia et al.](https://arxiv.org/abs/1806.01261)).
nodes.test: Hold out numbers and arrangements of objects, intervene on edges, and test predicted action consequences under new compositions.

nodes.name: Feed-forward & residual networks
nodes.authors: Rumelhart · Hinton · Williams; Amos · Kolter
nodes.text: General function composition can include constrained optimization layers. An explicit computational graph is not a semantic model.
nodes.handle: Explicit function composition provides a general learned map; optimization layers can embed constrained subproblems within it ([Rumelhart, Hinton, and Williams](https://www.nature.com/articles/323533a0), [Amos and Kolter](https://arxiv.org/abs/1703.00443)).
nodes.boundary: A differentiable computational graph is not a human semantic model; layer constraints cover their stated mathematical variables ([Amos and Kolter](https://arxiv.org/abs/1703.00443)).
nodes.test: Compare unconstrained prediction with an embedded feasible-action layer and test solver tolerances, infeasibility, and capability cost.

nodes.name: Dimensionality reduction
nodes.authors: Saxe · McClelland · Ganguli
nodes.text: Reduced representations must preserve the distinctions needed for actions and constraints, not only ordinary prediction.
nodes.handle: Low-dimensional representations can simplify learning or dynamics; singular-mode analysis gives a controlled example ([Saxe et al.](https://www.saxelab.org/assets/papers/Saxe2013a.pdf)).
nodes.boundary: Preserving high-variance directions is not the same objective as preserving controllable or safety-relevant distinctions; control uses input-output structure ([Åström and Murray](https://people.duke.edu/~hpgavin/SystemID/References/Astrom-Feedback-2006.pdf)).
nodes.test: Compare prediction-optimal compression with action- and constraint-aware compression on rare, consequential states.

nodes.name: Energy-based associative dynamics
nodes.authors: John Hopfield
nodes.text: A specified energy construction supports convergence analysis. A stable attractor need not be the intended retrieved memory.
nodes.handle: Symmetric associative-memory constructions expose an energy function with decreasing dynamics under the specified update rule ([Hopfield](https://redwood.berkeley.edu/wp-content/uploads/2018/08/hopfield82.pdf)).
nodes.boundary: Convergence to an attractor does not guarantee convergence to the intended memory; the energy argument does not cover every asymmetric recurrent network ([Hopfield](https://redwood.berkeley.edu/wp-content/uploads/2018/08/hopfield82.pdf)).
nodes.test: Corrupt inputs, add spurious memories, and test whether energy descent predicts successful retrieval or merely stable wrong answers.

nodes.name: Additive & monotonic predictors
nodes.authors: Rudin; You · Ding · Canini · Pfeifer · Gupta
nodes.text: Design inspectable predictors and selected monotonic relations. A correct shape constraint still needs the correct task meaning.
nodes.handle: Interpretable-by-design modeling is an alternative to post-hoc explanations; deep lattice networks can guarantee selected monotonic relations ([Rudin](http://www.arxiv.org/abs/1811.10154), [You et al.](https://arxiv.org/abs/1709.06680)).
nodes.boundary: A monotonic relationship must be appropriate for the actual task; guaranteeing the wrong shape does not make the prediction correct ([You et al.](https://arxiv.org/abs/1709.06680)).
nodes.test: Compare compact additive/monotonic models with flexible baselines; test whether domain experts’ stated constraints hold under interventions.

nodes.name: Concept bottlenecks
nodes.authors: Koh · Nguyen · Tang · Mussmann · Pierson · Kim · Liang
nodes.text: Expose supervised concepts as editable intermediate predictions. Concept prediction, nuisance exclusion, and causal intervention are separate questions.
nodes.handle: Supervised concepts become explicit editable intermediate predictions ([Koh et al.](https://proceedings.mlr.press/v119/koh20a/koh20a.pdf)).
nodes.boundary: Model-level concept edits are not automatically interventions on reality; even concept-predictive channels can retain nuisance information ([Koh et al.](https://proceedings.mlr.press/v119/koh20a/koh20a.pdf), [Almudévar, Hernández-Lobato, and Ortega, 2026 version](https://arxiv.org/html/2506.04877v3)).
nodes.test: Test edit accuracy, side effects, nuisance leakage, and performance after replacing all concepts with verified values.

nodes.name: Causal representation learning
nodes.authors: Ahuja · Mahajan · Wang · Bengio
nodes.text: Interventions can reduce latent ambiguity under stated decoder and support conditions. This is not arbitrary semantic recovery.
nodes.handle: Appropriate intervention data and structural assumptions can reduce latent ambiguity; some results identify factors up to permutation, shift, and scaling ([Ahuja, Mahajan, Wang, and Bengio](https://proceedings.mlr.press/v202/ahuja23a/ahuja23a.pdf)).
nodes.boundary: Theorems use specified decoder/support/intervention conditions; arbitrary pixels, language, and real interventions do not automatically satisfy them ([Ahuja et al.](https://proceedings.mlr.press/v202/ahuja23a/ahuja23a.pdf)).
nodes.test: Use known intervention targets during training but hold out combinations and mechanisms; quantify ambiguity instead of requiring arbitrary coordinate agreement.

nodes.name: Contracting recurrent networks
nodes.authors: Revay · Wang · Manchester
nodes.text: Recurrent equilibrium networks can enforce well-posedness, contraction, and selected gain bounds through their parameterization.
nodes.handle: Parameterizations can enforce well-posedness, contraction, and selected incremental gain/passivity constraints during learning ([Revay, Wang, and Manchester](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2104.05942)).
nodes.boundary: State and input-output robustness are not semantic correctness; persistent-memory capability can conflict with uniform contraction ([Revay et al.](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2104.05942), [Miller and Hardt](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1805.10369)).
nodes.test: Learn real task dynamics at increasing complexity; compare robust utility and delayed memory against an equally tuned unconstrained model.

nodes.name: Port-Hamiltonian neural control
nodes.authors: Zakwan · Ferrari-Trecate
nodes.text: Energy storage, dissipation, and ports support conditional compositional control guarantees. Digital implementation needs separate checking.
nodes.handle: Energy storage, dissipation, and input-output ports support compositional control design ([Zakwan and Ferrari-Trecate](https://ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org/html/2403.17785)).
nodes.boundary: Closed-loop guarantees need compatible plant/interconnection assumptions; continuous-time gain does not automatically survive digital implementation ([Zakwan and Ferrari-Trecate](https://ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org/html/2403.17785)).
nodes.test: Test the discretized controller, sensor delays, contact, and non-passive components; verify both energy accounting and useful task completion.

nodes.name: Equivariant architectures
nodes.authors: Risi Kondor (reference)
nodes.text: A network can satisfy a specified symmetry by construction. Consistent transformation is not the same as accurate prediction.
nodes.handle: Specified transformation laws can hold by construction when all components respect the group action ([Kondor](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12541325/)).
nodes.boundary: Equivariance means the answer transforms consistently, not that it is accurate or that every task shares the symmetry ([Kondor](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12541325/)).
nodes.test: Rotate, translate, or permute the world and desired output together; separately test symmetry-breaking context such as gravity or fixed obstacles.

nodes.name: Constrained RL & safety filters
nodes.authors: Achiam et al.; Alshiekh et al.; Wabersich · Zeilinger
nodes.text: Expected-cost optimization, temporal shields, and predictive safety filters enforce different objects under different assumptions.
nodes.handle: Expected-cost optimization, temporal-logic shields, and predictive safety filters provide different constraint mechanisms ([Achiam et al.](https://proceedings.mlr.press/v70/achiam17a/achiam17a.pdf), [Alshiekh et al.](https://arxiv.org/abs/1708.08611), [Wabersich and Zeilinger](https://ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org/html/1812.05506)).
nodes.boundary: Expected discounted cost is not every-trajectory safety; filtering needs confidence bounds, feasibility, and a safe fallback ([Achiam et al.](https://proceedings.mlr.press/v70/achiam17a/achiam17a.pdf), [Wabersich and Zeilinger](https://ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org/html/1812.05506)).
nodes.test: Measure unsafe-success episodes and severity, plus utility lost through intervention; deliberately test model-confidence failure and fallback feasibility.

nodes.name: Preferences, RLHF & DPO
nodes.authors: Christiano et al.; Rafailov et al.; Hadfield-Menell et al.
nodes.text: Preferences shape behavior; assistance models represent uncertain objectives. Proxy optimization does not uniquely identify user intent.
nodes.handle: Preference data shapes behavior; DPO directly fits preference pairs, while CIRL models uncertainty about a human reward ([Christiano et al.](https://arxiv.org/abs/1706.03741), [Rafailov et al.](https://papers.baulab.info/papers/also/Rafailov-2023.pdf), [Hadfield-Menell et al.](https://arxiv.org/abs/1606.03137)).
nodes.boundary: Preferences and reward models are proxies; overoptimization and reward non-uniqueness obstruct an automatic inference of actual intent ([Gao, Schulman, and Hilton](https://arxiv.org/abs/2210.10760), [Rafailov et al.](https://papers.baulab.info/papers/also/Rafailov-2023.pdf)).
nodes.test: Hold out evaluators and preference contexts; test explicit corrections, ambiguity questions, proxy exploitation, and preserved capability.

nodes.name: LLMs & reasoning models
nodes.authors: Ouyang et al.; Guo et al.; Lightman et al.; Lake · Baroni
nodes.text: Build capability through pretraining, instructions, verifiable outcomes, and compositional curricula. Evaluate correction and capability together.
nodes.handle: Pretraining, instruction training, process feedback, verifiable-outcome RL, and compositional curricula provide different capability-building levers ([Ouyang et al.](https://arxiv.org/abs/2203.02155), [Lightman et al.](http://arxiv.org/abs/2305.20050), [Guo et al.](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12443585/), [Lake and Baroni](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/37880371/)).
nodes.boundary: Benchmark success, preference gains, and readable reasoning do not establish universal semantic control; even measured prompt controllability is task- and distribution-dependent ([Cheng et al.](https://arxiv.org/html/2601.05637v1)).
nodes.test: Train a model to learn unfamiliar rule systems; test held-out compositional tasks, verifier-correct solutions, conflicts, clarification, and persistent corrections at matched compute.

nodes.name: Vision-language models
nodes.authors: Radford et al.; Liu · Li · Wu · Lee
nodes.text: Learn language-addressable visual behavior. Similarity and fluent description do not certify grounded scene understanding.
nodes.handle: Contrastive image-text training and visual instruction tuning provide language-addressable visual behavior ([Radford et al.](https://cdn.openai.com/papers/Learning_Transferable_Visual_Models_From_Natural_Language.pdf), [Liu, Li, Wu, and Lee](https://arxiv.org/abs/2304.08485)).
nodes.boundary: Text-image similarity or an articulate answer does not establish causal scene understanding or correct grounding ([Radford et al.](https://cdn.openai.com/papers/Learning_Transferable_Visual_Models_From_Natural_Language.pdf)).
nodes.test: Separate perception, relational reasoning, instruction priority, and uncertainty tests; counterbalance text priors against visual evidence.

nodes.name: Vision-language-action models
nodes.authors: Brohan et al.; Kim et al.; Black et al.
nodes.text: Combine perception, language, and action generation. Valid action representations do not guarantee safe physical trajectories.
nodes.handle: RT-2 uses action tokens, OpenVLA fine-tunes a VLM for actions, and π₀ generates continuous action chunks through flow matching ([Brohan et al.](https://arxiv.org/html/2307.15818v1), [Kim et al.](https://github.com/openvla/openvla), [Black et al.](https://arxiv.org/html/2410.24164)).
nodes.boundary: Valid action tokens are not valid trajectories; physical skills and safety remain separate from transferred web semantics ([RT-2](https://arxiv.org/html/2307.15818v1), [Fan et al., SafeVLA-Bench](https://arxiv.org/html/2606.00773v3)).
nodes.test: Jointly score task success, instruction correctness, whole-trajectory safety, interruptions, and new embodiment transfer.

nodes.name: Video & latent world models
nodes.authors: Assran et al. (V-JEPA 2); Liang et al. (WorldLens)
nodes.text: Separate visual prediction from action-conditioned consequences, state persistence, and actual closed-loop performance.
nodes.handle: V-JEPA 2 separates action-free visual pretraining from action-conditioned robotic post-training ([Assran et al.](https://ai.meta.com/research/publications/v-jepa-2-self-supervised-video-models-enable-understanding-prediction-and-planning/)).
nodes.boundary: Video plausibility and scene metrics need not translate into reliable closed-loop action consequences ([Liang et al., WorldLens](https://openaccess.thecvf.com/content/CVPR2026/papers/Liang_WorldLens_Full-Spectrum_Evaluations_of_Driving_World_Models_in_Real_World_CVPR_2026_paper.pdf)).
nodes.test: Intervene on actions, camera visibility, object identity, and hidden state; compare predicted consequences to actual held-out rollouts.

nodes.name: Object-centric world models
nodes.authors: Locatello et al.; Battaglia et al.
nodes.text: Slots and relations provide a construction for compositional scene models. Object identity and causal meaning still need tests.
nodes.handle: Slot Attention creates exchangeable object-oriented slots; graph models provide relational structure ([Locatello et al.](https://arxiv.org/abs/2006.15055), [Battaglia et al.](https://arxiv.org/abs/1806.01261)).
nodes.boundary: A slot is not guaranteed to be a persistent physical object or a causally identified variable ([Locatello et al.](https://arxiv.org/abs/2006.15055), [Ahuja et al.](https://proceedings.mlr.press/v202/ahuja23a/ahuja23a.pdf)).
nodes.test: Occlude and re-identify objects; change their properties and interactions; test object count, persistence, and controlled relation changes.

nodes.name: Neural-symbolic & program learning
nodes.authors: Ellis et al.; Trinh · Wu · Le · He · Luong
nodes.text: Learn proposals and reusable programs while checking explicit deductions. Coverage, translation, and search remain constraints.
nodes.handle: DreamCoder learns reusable program libraries; AlphaGeometry combines a learned proposer with symbolic deduction ([Ellis and collaborators](https://royalsocietypublishing.org/doi/10.1098/rsta.2022.0050), [Trinh, Wu, Le, He, and Luong](https://research.google/pubs/solving-olympiad-geometry-without-human-demonstrations/)).
nodes.boundary: Executable structure makes some computations inspectable, but specification coverage, search cost, and translation into the formal domain remain limits ([DreamCoder](https://royalsocietypublishing.org/doi/10.1098/rsta.2022.0050), [AlphaGeometry](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41586-023-06747-5)).
nodes.test: Learn reusable rules on unfamiliar tasks, then test novel compositions, deliberately wrong formalizations, and proof/checker failures.

nodes.name: Retrieval & explicit memory
nodes.authors: Lewis et al.; Wallace et al.
nodes.text: Separate external knowledge from model parameters. Evidence provenance and instruction authority require distinct checks.
nodes.handle: Retrieval-augmented generation combines learned parameters with an external document index ([Lewis et al.](https://proceedings.neurips.cc/paper_files/paper/2020/hash/6b493230205f780e1bc26945df7481e5-Abstract.html)).
nodes.boundary: Retrieved evidence can be stale, irrelevant, or contain untrusted instructions; instruction hierarchy needs separate treatment ([Lewis et al.](https://proceedings.neurips.cc/paper_files/paper/2020/hash/6b493230205f780e1bc26945df7481e5-Abstract.html), [Wallace et al.](https://openai.com/index/the-instruction-hierarchy/)).
nodes.test: Correct or delete a fact in memory, then test answer provenance, conflict handling, downstream actions, and resistance to malicious retrieved instructions.

nodes.name: Plant & system boundaries
nodes.authors: Åström · Murray
nodes.text: The plant is the system receiving control inputs. Its state, sensors, actuators, disturbances, timing, and environment define the control problem.
nodes.handle: Model the system as state dynamics plus a measurement map; connect physical-law and input/output descriptions. [Research reference](https://people.duke.edu/~hpgavin/SystemID/References/Astrom-Feedback-2006.pdf)
nodes.boundary: A model is a question-dependent approximation. An accurate component model is not automatically an accurate closed-loop deployment model. [Scope reference](https://people.duke.edu/~hpgavin/SystemID/References/Astrom-Feedback-2006.pdf)
nodes.test: Draw the full state/action/measurement boundary, then test omitted delays, saturation, memory, disturbances, and execution failures.

nodes.name: System identification
nodes.authors: Åström · Murray; Brunton · Dawson · Rowley
nodes.text: Infer a dynamical model from input/output experiments, with excitation and validation appropriate to its intended use.
nodes.handle: Design input/output experiments and estimate prediction models; validate on different trajectories before closing the loop. [Research reference](https://faculty.washington.edu/sbrunton/papers/BrDaRo2014.pdf)
nodes.boundary: ERA requires suitable Markov parameters; the aerodynamic study removes nondecaying components before identification. A fit is not global correctness. [Scope reference](https://faculty.washington.edu/sbrunton/papers/BrDaRo2014.pdf)
nodes.test: Compare linear, sparse, kernel, and neural models on unseen actions, multi-step rollout, calibration, and closed-loop control.

nodes.name: Reachability & controllability
nodes.authors: Kalman; Åström · Murray
nodes.text: Ask whether allowed inputs can steer state. For finite-dimensional LTI systems, matrix rank provides an exact unconstrained test.
nodes.handle: Use the rank of [B, AB, …, Aⁿ⁻¹B] for the LTI pair and calculate required input energy or feasible trajectories. [Research reference](https://people.duke.edu/~hpgavin/SystemID/References/Astrom-Feedback-2006.pdf)
nodes.boundary: Full rank does not imply cheap, bounded, safe, or semantically meaningful control. Nonlinear reachability is a different problem. [Scope reference](https://people.duke.edu/~hpgavin/SystemID/References/Astrom-Feedback-2006.pdf)
nodes.test: Test target-state transfer under actual actuator bounds and deadlines, not only the unconstrained rank criterion.

nodes.name: Observability & state observers
nodes.authors: Kalman; Åström · Murray
nodes.text: Ask whether input/output histories distinguish states. Observer design adds an estimator with its own noise and model assumptions.
nodes.handle: Use the observability matrix and design an observer so estimation-error dynamics decay for the specified linear model. [Research reference](https://people.duke.edu/~hpgavin/SystemID/References/Astrom-Feedback-2006.pdf)
nodes.boundary: Mathematical distinguishability does not guarantee useful accuracy with noisy sensors, weak signals, or model error. [Scope reference](https://people.duke.edu/~hpgavin/SystemID/References/Astrom-Feedback-2006.pdf)
nodes.test: Estimate states using held-out trajectories and sensor dropouts; compare error, uncertainty calibration, and control success.

nodes.name: Reachability & observability Gramians
nodes.authors: Moore; Scherpen · Rowley
nodes.text: Response-energy matrices quantify input-to-state and state-to-output behavior over a declared horizon.
nodes.handle: For a stable LTI model solve Lyapunov equations, relate reachability to input energy, and observability to output energy. [Research reference](https://personal.math.vt.edu/jborggaa/nlromc/Scherpen_NLROMc_tutorial.pdf)
nodes.boundary: Infinite-horizon Gramians require stability. Separate Gramian eigenvalues depend on state coordinates and all results depend on chosen inputs and outputs. [Scope reference](https://personal.math.vt.edu/jborggaa/nlromc/Scherpen_NLROMc_tutorial.pdf)
nodes.test: Compare finite-horizon energy predictions with actual interventions, after fixing state units, output weighting, and input costs.

nodes.name: Hankel operators & singular values
nodes.authors: Moore · Enns · Glover; Scherpen
nodes.text: The Hankel operator maps past inputs to future outputs. Stable LTI Hankel values are √eig(Wc Wo), not learning coefficients.
nodes.handle: Measure jointly reachable and observable dynamics through a coordinate-invariant Hankel singular spectrum. [Research reference](https://personal.math.vt.edu/jborggaa/nlromc/Scherpen_NLROMc_tutorial.pdf)
nodes.boundary: The spectrum depends on the input/output operator and its units. It does not rank semantic importance or directly measure loss-volume geometry. [Scope reference](https://personal.math.vt.edu/jborggaa/nlromc/Scherpen_NLROMc_tutorial.pdf)
nodes.test: Alter output scaling and verify that Hankel values change while a regular model's theoretical learning exponent remains fixed.

nodes.name: Balanced truncation
nodes.authors: Bruce Moore · Dale Enns · Keith Glover
nodes.text: Balance state reachability and observability, then reduce stable linear systems by discarding low-Hankel-value directions.
nodes.handle: For stable minimal LTI realizations with an appropriate truncation gap, obtain a stable reduced model and a twice-tail-sum error bound. [Research reference](https://lall.stanford.edu/engr210a/lectures/lecture11_2001_11_07_01.pdf)
nodes.boundary: The bound concerns induced input/output gain. It is not a general nonlinear, semantic, closed-loop, or rare-event guarantee. [Scope reference](https://lall.stanford.edu/engr210a/lectures/lecture11_2001_11_07_01.pdf)
nodes.test: Compare balanced reduction against PCA, magnitude and random reduction at matched order; measure task outputs and closed-loop behavior.

nodes.name: Nonlinear balancing & empirical Gramians
nodes.authors: Jacquelien Scherpen; Sanjay Lall · Jerrold Marsden · Sonja Glavaški
nodes.text: Extend reduction through nonlinear energy functions or response-based empirical Gramians, with different assumptions from LTI balancing.
nodes.handle: Estimate empirical controllability and observability Gramians from defined interventions; the construction recovers standard Gramians for stable linear systems. [Research reference](https://www.cmor-faculty.rice.edu/~cox/neuro/lall_2002a.pdf)
nodes.boundary: Nonlinear results depend on region, input amplitudes, sampling and coordinates. Do not attach the LTI tail bound without a suitable theorem. [Scope reference](https://www.cmor-faculty.rice.edu/~cox/neuro/lall_2002a.pdf)
nodes.test: Repeat reduction over operating regions and intervention amplitudes; quantify prediction and control failures under distribution shift.

nodes.name: Balanced POD & response snapshots
nodes.authors: Clarence W. Rowley
nodes.text: Direct and adjoint response snapshots support scalable approximate balancing of large systems.
nodes.handle: Use a cross-snapshot SVD and biorthogonal projection to approximate balanced coordinates without forming full dense Gramians. [Research reference](https://cwrowley.princeton.edu/papers/bt_ijbc3.pdf)
nodes.boundary: Ordinary POD prioritizes variance, not necessarily controllable and observable dynamics. Snapshot coverage and adjoint access matter. [Scope reference](https://cwrowley.princeton.edu/papers/bt_ijbc3.pdf)
nodes.test: Compare POD and balanced POD on the same plant, retained order, sensors, and actuators; measure input/output response error.

nodes.name: ERA & Hankel realization
nodes.authors: Jer-Nan Juang · Richard S. Pappa
nodes.text: Eigensystem realization identifies reduced dynamical models from response data using a Hankel-matrix SVD.
nodes.handle: Construct models for modal identification and model reduction from experimental response data. [Research reference](https://ntrs.nasa.gov/citations/19850022899)
nodes.boundary: A finite noisy Hankel matrix is not the ideal infinite operator. Order choice, excitation, sampling and preprocessing affect the inferred dynamics. [Scope reference](https://ntrs.nasa.gov/citations/19850022899)
nodes.test: Recover a held-out system from finite noisy data; vary horizons and noise, and compare forecast and controller performance.

nodes.name: Fisher information & identifiability
nodes.authors: Rafieisakhaei · Chakravorty · Kumar; Watanabe · Lau et al.
nodes.text: Information quantifies likelihood sensitivity to a named unknown. Initial-state information matches a noise-weighted observability Gramian in a specified Gaussian experiment.
nodes.handle: Derive an information matrix from the likelihood; distinguish initial-state estimation from parameter identification. [Research reference](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1801.09877)
nodes.boundary: Unweighted observability alone ignores measurement covariance, process noise, and prior information. State Fisher information is not automatically parameter Fisher information. [Scope reference](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1801.09877)
nodes.test: Check the weighted-Gramian equality in a linear Gaussian experiment, then add process noise and test the breakdown of the simpler approximation.

nodes.name: Frequency-domain control: PID, Bode, Nyquist
nodes.authors: Nyquist · Bode; Åström · Murray
nodes.text: Analyze feedback loops through frequency response, gain and phase, disturbance sensitivity, delay, and stability margins.
nodes.handle: Use loop shaping and PID design with gain/phase margins, sensor-noise analysis and anti-windup where actuators saturate. [Research reference](https://people.duke.edu/~hpgavin/SystemID/References/Astrom-Feedback-2006.pdf)
nodes.boundary: Frequency-domain LTI calculations do not directly certify arbitrary nonlinear learned policies or unknown changes to the plant. [Scope reference](https://people.duke.edu/~hpgavin/SystemID/References/Astrom-Feedback-2006.pdf)
nodes.test: Measure step and frequency responses with realistic delay, noise and saturation; compare against a learned controller at matched latency.

nodes.name: LQR & optimal state feedback
nodes.authors: Kalman; Åström · Murray
nodes.text: Choose linear feedback to optimize a declared quadratic state-and-action objective for linear dynamics.
nodes.handle: Solve a Riccati equation under the relevant stabilizability and detectability conditions; use as a transparent model-based baseline. [Research reference](https://people.duke.edu/~hpgavin/SystemID/References/Astrom-Feedback-2006.pdf)
nodes.boundary: Quadratic cost is the engineer's specification, not a complete description of user intent. Constraints and model mismatch need additional treatment. [Scope reference](https://people.duke.edu/~hpgavin/SystemID/References/Astrom-Feedback-2006.pdf)
nodes.test: Compare learned control with LQR on matched dynamics; add uncertainty and constraints rather than silently changing the benchmark.

nodes.name: LQG & the separation principle
nodes.authors: Kalman · Bucy; Åström · Murray
nodes.text: Combine linear-quadratic control and Gaussian state estimation under the assumptions of the LQG problem.
nodes.handle: Pair a Kalman estimator with an LQR controller for the specified linear stochastic system. [Research reference](https://people.duke.edu/~hpgavin/SystemID/References/Astrom-Feedback-2006.pdf)
nodes.boundary: Separation does not generally transfer to nonlinear learning, unknown parameters, or arbitrary perception/policy pipelines. [Scope reference](https://people.duke.edu/~hpgavin/SystemID/References/Astrom-Feedback-2006.pdf)
nodes.test: Compare separated design with belief-aware control when dynamics are uncertain; track task cost and estimation error.

nodes.name: Robust control & small-gain analysis
nodes.authors: Åström · Murray (reference synthesis)
nodes.text: Design and analyze feedback under declared model uncertainty, using sensitivity, gain bounds, and structured assumptions.
nodes.handle: Use sensitivity functions and small-gain conditions to budget robustness of specified interconnections. [Research reference](https://people.duke.edu/~hpgavin/SystemID/References/Astrom-Feedback-2006.pdf)
nodes.boundary: Unmodeled uncertainty, missing delays, or a bypassed intervention path lie outside the certificate. [Scope reference](https://people.duke.edu/~hpgavin/SystemID/References/Astrom-Feedback-2006.pdf)
nodes.test: Stress-test the declared uncertainty set and explicitly test just outside it; record capability and robustness trade-offs.

nodes.name: Model predictive control & safety filters
nodes.authors: Kim P. Wabersich · Melanie N. Zeilinger
nodes.text: Optimize a model-predicted action sequence, execute a step, and replan; safety filtering adds confidence, feasibility and fallback requirements.
